step3.title: Create a vault and upload.
step3.text: A vault is a private repo on your account. Make as many as you need.

features.lead: Everything you expect from a file drive:

free.title: No subscription.
free.text: GitHub gives you private repositories for free. GitVault uses them.

yours.title: Your files stay yours.
yours.text: They live in repos on your account. Stop using GitVault tomorrow and they're still there.

history.title: Every change is saved.
history.text: Git keeps the history of every file.

cost.a: No. GitVault is free, and private repos are free on GitHub's free plan.

storage.a: As much as you want, spread across vaults. GitHub recommends keeping each repo under 1–5 GB: when a vault fills up, create another one.

fileSize.q: Is there a file size limit?
fileSize.a: Yes: 100 MB per file, a hard GitHub limit.

bulk.q: Can I upload thousands of files at once?
bulk.a: You can, but GitHub limits how fast. Big uploads take time.

privacy.a: Your vaults are private: only you. GitHub hosts them, so GitHub's privacy terms apply.

access.q: Can GitVault access my other repositories?
access.a: GitHub asks you to grant access to your repositories, but GitVault only shows and changes repos tagged with the {topic} topic. Everything else stays untouched.

existing.q: Can I use a repo I already have?
existing.a: Yes. Add the {topic} topic to it on GitHub and it shows up as a vault.

leave.q: What happens if I stop using GitVault?
leave.a: Nothing. Your files stay in your repos on GitHub.

final.title: Your free drive is one click away.
